title: What a data dictionary is and why it is used

learning_objectives.text: explain the purpose of a data dictionary

lesson_objectives.all: define a data dictionary and list the items it records for each field
lesson_objectives.most: explain how a data dictionary keeps a database consistent and who uses it
lesson_objectives.some: describe the metadata of real fields and explain which problems a data dictionary prevents for a given organisation

descriptors: states that a data dictionary describes the structure of a database (metadata)

assessment_criteria.criterion: Identify the items recorded for each field
descriptors: names at least five items: field name, data type, size, format, key, validation, description, example
chooses a suitable data type for a field and justifies it

assessment_criteria.criterion: Explain the purpose of a data dictionary
descriptors: explains how it keeps field names and types consistent so tables can be linked
explains how recorded validation rules protect data integrity
names who uses it and for what

learners_can: define a term precisely (A data dictionary is a … that …)
explain a purpose with cause and effect (so that, which means, therefore)
describe a field using subject vocabulary
phrases: A data dictionary is a document that …
The field … has the data type … because …
Without a data dictionary, …, which means …
The tester / programmer uses it to …

values.action: Groups carefully describe every field of their client's table and check each other's work for accuracy, as real database designers do.
Groups present their data dictionary entries and give and accept peer feedback (two stars and a wish).
Learners discuss their responsibility for describing citizens' personal data correctly in school, clinic and government databases of Kazakhstan.

cross_curricular: English: precise definitions and technical descriptions.
Mathematics: choosing between integer and real numbers, ranges for validation.
Business studies: documentation in real projects and the cost of errors.
ict: ICT Practice Platform, Lessons section: theory as slides, live polls and tasks, pair and group work on shared laptops.
Practice questions with automatic feedback; results visible to the teacher live.
Example of a real system catalogue (information_schema) shown on the board.
previous_learning: Basic concepts of a database: tables, records, fields, data types, primary and foreign keys. Entity-relationship diagram: entities, attributes and relationships drawn at the design stage.
safety: Move to the group's laptop calmly; keep bags and cables off the floor.
Laptops stay on the desk; short screen break between the two halves of the lesson.

support: Key words with definitions on the title slide; sentence frames for explanations.
Worked example: the Students table and its data dictionary on the slides before the pair task.
The group task has labelled boxes for each item of the data dictionary.
Random mixed-ability groups with roles: leader, writer, presenter, checker.
stretch: Explain the difference between an active and a passive data dictionary with an example.
Suggest a validation rule for every field of the client's table and justify it.
Explain why CHAR(3) is better than VARCHAR(30) for a class code.

assessment: Live results of every task on the teacher's slide: misconceptions are discussed at once.
Polls and together tasks check understanding before the next step opens.
Peer assessment of the group's data dictionary entries against the success criteria.
Exit ticket (marked automatically) checks the three lesson objectives.
Practice results count towards SAU points; the group task is checked by the teacher with feedback in the lesson.

blocks.title: Hook: what does DOB mean?
blocks.teacher: Shows the objectives, then asks: a new programmer finds a field called DOB with no documentation. Which value should be stored? Learners vote; the different answers show why a database needs a data dictionary.
blocks.learners: Vote on their laptops and explain their choice.

poll.question: A field is called DOB and nobody has documented it. Which value should it store?
options: Any of them — we cannot know

resources: Title slide: objectives and key words

blocks.title: Starter: recall tables, keys and ERDs
blocks.teacher: Opens three quick questions on previous topics and corrects the most common mistake.

blocks.title: Slides: what a data dictionary is
blocks.teacher: Presents data and metadata, the items of a data dictionary, data types, naming rules and the design stage. Together task: which item of the data dictionary is DD/MM/YYYY? Class votes and discusses.
blocks.learners: Follow the slides, vote in the together task and give examples of metadata.
resources: Theory: What a data dictionary is (slides)

blocks.title: Pair work: items and data types
blocks.teacher: Opens the pair task: random pairs, one laptop each. Monitors live results and helps pairs that are stuck.
blocks.learners: Work in random pairs on one laptop: five practice questions on metadata, items and data types.

blocks.title: Slides: the purpose of a data dictionary
blocks.teacher: Presents why a data dictionary is used, who uses it, the mismatched-key example, active and passive dictionaries and how it differs from an ERD. Together task: what goes wrong when StudentID is Text in one table and Integer in another?
blocks.learners: Vote and explain using "Without a data dictionary, …, which means …".
slides: The purpose of a data dictionary
resources: Theory: The purpose of a data dictionary (slides)

blocks.title: Individual practice: purpose and users
blocks.teacher: Opens four questions on the purpose; checks the live results.

blocks.title: Group work: database designers
blocks.teacher: Opens the group task: random groups of four, each with a client table and the host's laptop. After 12 minutes two groups present (1 minute each); the others give feedback against the success criteria. Teacher can ask for the answers to be checked during the lesson.
blocks.learners: In groups, write the data dictionary entries for three fields of the client's table and explain two problems the dictionary prevents for this client.
resources: Live task: group data dictionary with client cards

blocks.title: Exit ticket
blocks.teacher: Opens the exit ticket and uses the results to plan lesson 2.

blocks.title: Reflection and homework
blocks.teacher: Learners rate their confidence (traffic light). Homework: finish the remaining lesson 1 practice and hand in handwritten notes for lesson 1.
blocks.learners: Rate their confidence and note the homework.

poll.question: How confident are you with today's objectives?
options: Green: I can define it, list the items and explain its purpose
Amber: I can define it and list the items

dd-l1-scenarios.details: Table Orders: OrderID, StudentID, MealName, Price, OrderDate, Paid. About 300 orders a day; parents pay online.
Table Tickets: TicketID, FilmTitle, ShowDate, SeatNumber, Price, IsChild. Tickets are sold online and at the desk.
Table Members: MemberID, Surname, DateOfBirth, Phone, JoinDate, IsStudent. Members can join from age 10.
Table Appointments: AppointmentID, PatientID, DoctorID, AppointmentDate, Time, Confirmed. Patients book by phone.
Table Books: ISBN, Title, Author, YearPublished, Copies, OnLoan. The library has 8 000 books.

live_tasks.title: A record
live_tasks.text: In a table of students, what is one **record**?

options.content: All the data about one student (one row)

live_tasks.title: A foreign key
live_tasks.text: `Loans` contains the field `StudentID`, which is the primary key of `Students`. In `Loans`, `StudentID` is …

options.content: the records stored in each table
the entities and the relationships between them
the SQL code of the queries

live_tasks.title: DD/MM/YYYY
live_tasks.text: In a data dictionary, `DD/MM/YYYY` is written for the field `DateOfBirth`. Which item is it?

scheme.explanation: The format says how the data is entered and shown; the data type is Date.

live_tasks.title: Two different keys
live_tasks.text: `StudentID` is Text in `Students` but Integer in `Loans`. What is the result?

options.content: The tables cannot be linked correctly, so reports miss students' names

scheme.explanation: A primary key and its foreign key must have the same data type and size — the data dictionary makes sure they do.

live_tasks.title: Database designers
live_tasks.text: Your group designs the database for your client (see your card). Write the data dictionary entries for **three** fields of the client's table, then explain **two** problems the data dictionary prevents for this client.

fields.label: Field 1: name · data type · size · format · key · validation · example
Field 2: name · data type · size · format · key · validation · example
Field 3: name · data type · size · format · key · validation · example
Two problems the data dictionary prevents for this client

scheme.mark_scheme:
Each field (max 2 each, 6 in all): a suitable data type and size (1); a suitable format / key / validation and an example consistent with the type (1)
Problems prevented (2): e.g. the same field gets different types in different tables so the tables cannot be linked; invalid data such as a negative price or a wrong date is accepted; programmers / new staff misunderstand a field; dates in different formats

points.criterion: Field 1: suitable format / key / validation and example
Field 2: suitable format / key / validation and example
Field 3: suitable format / key / validation and example
Two problems prevented, linked to the client

scheme.model_answer: School canteen. OrderID · Integer · — · — · PK · presence, unique · 10452. Price · Real / Decimal(6,2) · — · 0.00 · — · range 0–5000 · 850.00. OrderDate · Date · 10 · DD/MM/YYYY · — · not in the future · 05/11/2026. Problems: StudentID would have the same type in Orders and Students, so each order is linked to the right pupil; the range check on Price stops a typing error such as 85000 from charging parents too much.

options.content: The field Surname is Text with a maximum of 30 characters

live_tasks.title: Data integrity
live_tasks.text: How does a data dictionary help to keep data **accurate**?

options.content: It records validation rules, so invalid values are rejected
It makes a backup every night

live_tasks.title: Not in a data dictionary
live_tasks.text: Which of these is **not** normally recorded in a data dictionary for a field?

options.content: The value stored in every record

scheme.explanation: The values are the data itself; the dictionary only describes the fields.
